title: Microsoft Purview: allow version trimming for content under retention in SharePoint and OneDrive
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned retention override from today's version-management controls. The roadmap dates, licensing qualifications, admin path and PowerShell calls are supported; searches found no documentation of the new setting's controls or feature-specific licensing.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[1].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Today's library version limits are ignored for items under a retention policy until the retention period is reached.
claims.quote: For items that are subject to a retention policy (or an eDiscovery hold), the versioning limits for the document library are ignored until the retention period of the document is reached (or the eDiscovery hold is released).

claims.claim: Today's library version limits are ignored for items on an eDiscovery hold until the hold is released.
claims.quote: For items that are subject to a retention policy (or an eDiscovery hold), the versioning limits for the document library are ignored until the retention period of the document is reached (or the eDiscovery hold is released).

claims.claim: Old versions of retained content are not automatically purged under today's behavior.
claims.quote: In this scenario, old versions aren't automatically purged

claims.claim: Users are prevented from deleting versions of content subject to the retention policy.
claims.quote: In this scenario, old versions aren't automatically purged and users are prevented from deleting versions.

claims.claim: Microsoft intends the setting to reclaim storage occupied by retained file versions without removing retention policies.
claims.quote: SharePoint/compliance admins at large, regulated enterprises must cap and reclaim storage consumed by retained file versions, while keeping legal-hold and records promises intact.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes version cleanup, not new data access.
claims.quote: When turned on, SharePoint’s version management will be permitted to trim file versions per the defined limits except for specific protected cases.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Versions deleted by trimming jobs are permanently deleted.
claims.quote: Versions deleted by using trimming jobs are permanently deleted. This deletion workflow bypasses the normal recycle bin retention

claims.claim: Recovery of trimmed versions requires a preexisting backup, such as Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.quote: deleted versions can't be recovered unless the data was previously backed up by using Microsoft 365 Backup or a similar backup solution.

claims.claim: A trim job encountering a version under a retention policy stamps an expiration date instead of deleting it.
claims.quote: When a trim job encounters a version under a retention policy or an eDiscovery hold, it will stamp an expiration date on the version instead of deleting it.

claims.claim: A trim job encountering a version under an eDiscovery hold stamps an expiration date instead of deleting it.
claims.quote: When a trim job encounters a version under a retention policy or an eDiscovery hold, it will stamp an expiration date on the version instead of deleting it.

claims.claim: Organization-level version defaults apply to newly created libraries rather than updating existing libraries.
claims.quote: Changes made to organization-level version history limits apply to new SharePoint libraries and OneDrive user accounts created since the change was made.

claims.claim: Organization-level version defaults also apply to new OneDrive accounts.

claims.claim: Changing organization-level version defaults does not trim existing versions.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The automatic default is at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Version history limits > Automatically.
claims.quote: Go to Settings in the SharePoint admin center ... Select Version History limits. Select Automatically.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $true configures automatic tenant version defaults.
claims.quote: To set Automatic version history limits for all new document libraries created in your organization using PowerShell, run the following command: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $true

claims.claim: Manual tenant version limits use the Set-SPOTenant -MajorVersionLimit parameter.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant `
    -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $false `
    -MajorVersionLimit <int> `
    -ExpireVersionsAfterDays <int, 0 for no expiration>

claims.claim: Manual tenant expiration limits use the Set-SPOTenant -ExpireVersionsAfterDays parameter.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant `
    -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $false `
    -MajorVersionLimit <int> `
    -ExpireVersionsAfterDays <int, 0 for no expiration>
